title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
summary: You have n computers and a battery array where each element represents the minutes a battery can run a single computer.
statement: You have n computers and a battery array where each element represents the minutes a battery can run a single computer. You can transfer batteries between computers at any time without delay. The goal is to determine the maximum number of minutes you can run all n computers simultaneously, given that batteries cannot be recharged.
constraints: There are at least n batteries and battery swaps are instantaneous.
One battery powers at most one computer at a time, but its charge may contribute across computers over time.
Return the maximum whole minutes all n computers can run simultaneously.
reference_solution:
def maximum_computer_runtime(n,batteries):
    low,high=0,sum(batteries)//n
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high+1)//2
        if sum(min(value,middle) for value in batteries)>=n*middle:low=middle
        else:high=middle-1
    return low

hints: For a candidate time t, each battery can contribute at most t charge because it cannot power multiple computers simultaneously.
Feasibility is sum(min(b,t))>=n*t and is monotone, so binary-search t.
Search zero through total_charge//n for the greatest feasible integer.
The capped-charge condition is necessary and sufficient under free swapping, and monotonicity makes the upper-bound search exact.
